cars.name: BMW X5 Le Mans
search: BMW X5 V12 Le Mans prototype
cars.notes: One-off X5 with the 6.1 L V12 from the Le Mans-winning V12 LMR, about 700 hp. Lapped the Nürburgring Nordschleife in under 8 minutes with Hans-Joachim Stuck.

cars.name: Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR
cars.location: Mostly Mercedes-Benz, Stuttgart; one at the Cité de l'Automobile, Mulhouse
cars.notes:
W196S sports-racing car that won the 1955 World Sportscar Championship. Wikipedia: 9 chassis built, 7 open race cars and 2 coupés; one (0006/55) destroyed at Le Mans, so 8 survive. Sources disagree: Supercar Nostalgia says eight in some places and nine in others; Ultimatecarpage lists 0009/55 as never completed and 0010/55 as a test car.

Chassis 0007/55 and 0008/55 became the Uhlenhaut Coupés, tracked as their own entry (Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupé).

cars.name: 300 SLR 0001/54
cars.notes: The first 300 SLR. Moss 2nd at the 1955 Eifelrennen (#3), its only race. Shown for years at the Henry Ford Museum, Dearborn, then returned to Stuttgart.

cars.name: 300 SLR 0002/55
cars.notes: Development car and team spare (T-car at the Tourist Trophy and Targa Florio). Never raced. Registered AW 84 7984.

cars.name: 300 SLR 0003/55 "Fangio"
cars.notes: Fangio's car: 2nd in the Mille Miglia (#658, solo), won the Eifelrennen and the Swedish GP, 3rd at the Tourist Trophy, 2nd at the Targa Florio (Fangio/Kling), which clinched the 1955 title.

cars.name: 300 SLR 0004/55 "722"
cars.notes: Moss and Jenkinson won the 1955 Mille Miglia as #722, a record that still stands. Also won the Tourist Trophy (Moss/Fitch) and the Targa Florio (Moss/Collins). Raced in all six 1955 events and won three. Often called the most valuable car in the world.

cars.name: 300 SLR 0005/55 "Schlumpf"
cars.location: Cité de l'Automobile, Mulhouse, France (Schlumpf Collection)
cars.notes: Kling crashed out of the Mille Miglia (#701), 2nd at the Tourist Trophy (Fangio/Kling), 4th at the Targa Florio. Lent to the Schlumpf brothers in 1966; stayed after the French state bought the collection in 1981.

cars.name: 300 SLR 0006/55 "Le Mans #20"
cars.notes: Pierre Levegh / John Fitch, #20. Destroyed in the 1955 Le Mans disaster, which killed Levegh and 83 spectators. Earlier crashed by Herrmann in the Mille Miglia (#704). The sources don't say what became of the wreckage.

cars.name: 300 SLR 0010/55 "test car"
cars.notes: Listed only by Ultimatecarpage: the last 300 SLR built in 1955, used to test new parts, never raced. Supercar Nostalgia doesn't list it.

cars.name: Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupé
cars.location: One at the Mercedes-Benz Museum, Stuttgart. The other sold in 2022 for €135M to a private collector.
cars.notes: Only two prototypes were ever made—one nicknamed "Red" (chassis 8) and the other "Blue" (chassis 7), differentiated by their interior upholstery colors.  In May 2022, Mercedes-Benz sold the red Uhlenhaut Coupé at a private RM Sotheby's auction for €135 million (roughly $142–143 million), making it the most expensive car ever sold in history. The proceeds went toward the global Mercedes-Benz Fund for environmental and decarbonization scholarships. The second car ("Blue") remains in the collection of the Mercedes-Benz Museum in Stuttgart

cars.name: Uhlenhaut Coupé "Red"
cars.location: Private collector (sold May 2022, RM Sotheby's private auction, €135M)
cars.notes: Chassis 8, red interior.

cars.name: Uhlenhaut Coupé "Blue"
cars.notes: Chassis 7, blue interior.

cars.name: McLaren F1 LM
cars.location: Brunei Royal Family (3), McLaren (prototype), Ralph Lauren (1), Japan (1)
cars.notes:
Six built: the XP LM prototype plus five customer cars, LM1 to LM5 (spring and summer 1996). Built to honour the five F1 GTRs that finished the 1995 Le Mans 24 Hours, including the winner, and to homologate the 1996 GTR. £680,000 plus tax new, £40,000 more than a standard F1. Unrestricted GTR BMW S70/2 6.1 L V12, 680 bhp, 1,062 kg, 225 mph.

Not original LMs: standard F1s 018 and 073 were later upgraded by the factory to "LM-specification". 018 sold for $19,805,000 at RM Sotheby's Monterey 2019; 073 sold for about $13.75M at RM Sotheby's in 2015. Articles about them will show up here because they say "F1 LM".

cars.name: McLaren F1 XP LM (prototype)
cars.notes: The prototype, in Historic Orange. Unveiled at Woking in December 1995 and used in the original publicity photos. Never sold. Ron Dennis reportedly promised it to Lewis Hamilton if he won three titles with McLaren; he won one (2008).

cars.name: McLaren F1 LM1
cars.notes: Black over pale grey with blue, yellow and pale grey stripes. Dark grey Alcantara with yellow highlights. Registered KF90 in Brunei. In the Brunei Royal collection since new (Supercar Nostalgia, June 2025).

cars.name: McLaren F1 LM2
cars.location: Last named owner Yoshio Tsuzuki, ZAZ Museum, Nagoya (unconfirmed)
cars.notes: Historic Orange. First owner Yoshio Tsuzuki (ZENT CEO), shown at his ZAZ Museum in Nagoya next to his F1 053, GTR 13R and F1 GT 58F1GT. No recent source confirms he still owns it, and the Supercar Nostalgia LM2 page is gone (404).

cars.name: McLaren F1 LM3
cars.notes: Historic Orange, registered 1 SEN. David Morrison took delivery 12 August 1996 and drove it in the first Gumball 3000 (1999). Frank Selldorff 2003, Ralph Lauren 2004, still with him (Supercar Nostalgia, January 2024).

cars.name: McLaren F1 LM4
cars.notes: Black over pale grey with blue, yellow and pale grey stripes, like LM1. Registered BP75 in Brunei. Nominal mileage since new (Supercar Nostalgia, December 2024).

cars.name: McLaren F1 LM5
cars.notes: Historic Orange. Registered BM2208 in Brunei. Nominal mileage since new (Supercar Nostalgia, April 2025).

cars.name: Jaguar XJ220 S
cars.location: Private collections; last known sale London 2022
cars.notes:
TWR's lightweight road version of the XJ220: carbon bodywork except the doors, fixed perspex-covered headlights, front splitter, wider sills, adjustable rear wing, Kevlar seats, no stereo or air conditioning. 3.5 L twin-turbo V6, 680 hp (standard XJ220: 542 hp), about 1,050-1,080 kg, 0-60 mph in 3.3 s, 228 mph. Shown at the 1993 Autosport show.

How many: sources say 5 (HotCars, RM Sotheby's 2022) or 6 (RM Sotheby's 2012: five standard and one modified; Jaguar Enthusiasts Club; Supercars.net). Five chassis are named: 220779, 220784, 220793, 220802, 220803. The sixth, if it exists, is unidentified. 220801 is sometimes mentioned, but HotCars calls it a one-off TWR racer, not an S.

The XJ220 C race cars and the standard XJ220 are not tracked here.

The only orange XJ220 S (Outrageous Orange). Completed 21 April 1993, left-hand drive. Believed kept by TWR until sold to a Belgian collector in February 1998; to the USA November 1999 (Keuylian Motors via Michael Sheehan's European Auto Sales), sold again that month; via Ferraris-Online 2007, in California until 2012; Jasbir Dhillon 2012; shown at The Quail 2015; Gran Turismo Collection 2018. Sold for £933,125 at RM Sotheby's London 2022 (Lot 121) with 4,822 km.
cars.name: XJ220 S 220779 "Orange"

cars.location: Unknown; sold at RM Sotheby's Arizona 2012
cars.notes: Imported to California in silver; later matte black, then repainted Lamborghini Reventon Gray. TWR titanium exhaust, Infiniti projector headlights, refurbished magnesium wheels; shown at SEMA. Said to be the only XJ220 S with a US DOT/EPA certificate. Sold for $230,000 at RM Sotheby's Arizona 2012 (Lot 127).

Jaguar XJ220 Concept
cars.location: Jaguar Daimler Heritage Trust (inventory 95/J.50); photographed at the British Motor Museum, Gaydon (current display unconfirmed)
cars.notes: The one-off original XJ220. Idea by chief engineer Jim Randle (December 1984), designed by Keith Helfet, built by "the Saturday Club": about a dozen Jaguar engineers and designers working in their own time, helped by about forty suppliers. 6.2 L quad-cam V12, prototype four-wheel drive, Group C-based chassis, aluminium body. Unveiled by Sir John Egan at the Birmingham Motor Show (NEC), 18 October 1988. The production car (281 built 1992-1994) switched to a twin-turbo V6 and rear-wheel drive. Not road registered.

cars.name: Mercedes-Benz CLK GTR
cars.notes:
Road-going homologation version of the 1997-98 FIA GT championship winner (the race cars are not tracked here). 26 road cars: 20 coupés (plaques 01/25 to 20/25) and 6 roadsters (21/25 to 25/25, plus a sixth built later outside the count), after two factory prototypes/demonstrators. Plaques on the dash, centre console and door sills. Coupés built late 1998 to 1999 at about $1.5M; roadster years given as 2002 or 2006. 6.9 L V12 (about 612-623 hp), 6-speed sequential, 1,470 kg, 199 mph.

Super Sport: HWA later fitted the 7.3 L V12 (655-720 hp) to prototype 2 and coupés 01, 03, 13 and 17 (Supercar Nostalgia; Rare Cars Only also names 19).

VINs run WDB2973971Y0000NN; Ultimatecarpage says the first 11 went to race cars and prototypes, so 000012 is the first road car. Identifiers use "N of 25" rather than "NN/25" because search engines read "07/25" as a date.

Race-car articles also mention "CLK GTR", so they appear in this entry's own list.

cars.name: CLK GTR 1997 demonstrator
cars.notes: VIN WDBA2973971Y000002, plate LB-RA-204. One of two factory demonstrators (the other was LB-RA-100), used for magazine road tests and brochures; not one of the 25. Sold by HWA in 1999 to a friend of AMG founder Hans Werner Aufrecht; engine enlarged to 7.3 L in 2001 (over 700 bhp). Sold at Bonhams in August 2003 for just over €800,000 with 12,500 on the odometer.

cars.name: CLK GTR 01/25 "Super Sport"
cars.notes: VIN WDB2973971Y000012, the first customer road car. Super Sport (7.3 L, HWA). Sold new to the USA; offered by RM 2010/2012 with 1,335 miles ($1.1M listed by Ultimatecarpage).

cars.name: Porsche 911 GT1 Strassenversion
cars.location: Private collections; Porsche keeps the GT1-98 road car
cars.notes:
Road versions of Porsche's GT1 homologation race car (the race cars aren't tracked here).

1996 street prototypes with round 993-style headlights: 2 or 3 (Stuttcars and Sports Car Market say two; RM Sotheby's and Conceptcarz say chassis 001-003). 1997 production road cars with 996-style headlights: 20, chassis 004 to 022 (RM) or 023 (Conceptcarz). About $900,000 new ($912,000 per RM). 3.2 L water-cooled twin-turbo flat-six, 544 hp, about 192 mph, about 950 kg. 1998: one GT1-98 road car, built to homologate the 1998 race car, kept by Porsche.

Chassis 005 is the only road car with a public history. Total 911's and HotCars' pages on the model didn't load during research.

cars.name: 911 GT1 1996 prototype (Ministry test car)
cars.notes: One of the 993-headlight street prototypes. Delivered in early 1996 to the German Federal Ministry of Transport for road-approval testing, which it passed (Stuttcars). Chassis number (001-003) not stated.

cars.name: 911 GT1 1996 prototype (Khalid Abdul Rahim)
cars.notes: One of the 993-headlight street prototypes, owned by Bahrain collector Khalid Abdul Rahim (Stuttcars 2016 and 2017). Chassis number (001-003) not stated.

cars.name: 911 GT1 Strassenversion 005 "Kemper"
cars.location: UK (Brazilian industrialist, bought at Gooding Amelia Island 2017)
cars.notes: VIN WP0ZZZ99ZWS396005. Arctic Silver Metallic over black leather, air conditioning and comfort seat padding. Assembly finished January 1998; the second road car with 996-style headlights. First owner Tobias Kemper (Germany), delivered 29 May 1998 via Porsche Zentrum Munich Olympiapark, about 4,400 km. Don Wallace (Lazydays RV founder), Tampa, Florida, 2003/04; federalised under Show and Display by JK Technologies, said to be the only road GT1 legally imported to the US. Mark Wilson, Oldsmar, Florida, May 2009. Sold for $1,175,000 at RM Sotheby's Monterey 2012 (Lot 246). Manfred Freisinger, Germany, fall 2012. Back to the US 2015 (Michigan consignor). Sold for $5,665,000 at Gooding & Co. Amelia Island, 10 March 2017 (Lot 42), 7,900 km, then a record for any 911; buyer described as a Brazilian industrialist living in the UK (Sports Car Market). Probably the GT1 in the 2021 Carfection group test with CLK GTR 07/25 and a McLaren F1.

cars.name: Mercedes-Benz C111
cars.location: Mercedes-Benz (13 cars); one C111-II at auction February 2027
cars.notes:
Experimental cars, never sold, used 1969-1979 to test Wankel rotary engines, then diesel and turbo engines, with speed records at Nardò, Italy. Customers famously sent Mercedes blank cheques for one.

Wikipedia: 16 built (13 first- and second-generation Wankel cars, 2 C111-III, 1 C111-IV); other sources say 12 or 17. The first plastic-bodied 1969 prototype no longer exists (Secret Classics). Mercedes said in November 2026 that 17 were built: one was crash-tested and three dismantled in the 1970s, leaving 13 in its collection, none ever sold until C111-II "Car 33" was put up for auction (RM Sotheby's, Louvre, Paris, 3 February 2027). Mercedes has contractually committed not to sell another C111 for 25 years.

No source identifies individual cars by chassis or plate, so they're tracked by version below. Only the C111-IV is a single car.

cars.name: C111-I
cars.notes: 6 built (Supercar Nostalgia; Secret Classics says 7). Three-rotor Wankel (M950F), about 275-280 hp, about 162 mph. First prototypes metallic white, then "Weissherbst" orange. Press demos at Hockenheim 1-5 September 1969, public debut at Frankfurt that month. One was built with a 250 bhp M117 V8 for comparison. Secret Classics: only two survive, one restyled to look like a C111-II (shown at Techno Classica, April 2019).

cars.name: C111-II
cars.notes: 7 built (Supercar Nostalgia; Secret Classics says Mercedes owns "all six"). Four-rotor Wankel, about 350 hp, 186 mph, 0-62 mph in 4.8 s. Shown at Geneva, March 1970. One had a 300 bhp M117 V8 and one an automatic gearbox. Orange and black check interior. One is shown at the Mercedes-Benz Museum, Stuttgart. "Car 33" (below) is going to auction in February 2027, the first C111 ever sold.

cars.name: C111-II "Car 33"
cars.location: Mercedes-Benz Museum, Stuttgart; RM Sotheby's auction at the Louvre, Paris, 3 February 2027
cars.notes:
The first C111 Mercedes has ever sold. 1970 C111-II, orange, gull-wing doors, four-rotor Wankel (M950), 350 PS, up to 300 km/h; plate S-Y 6200. Shown in the museum foyer from 2006; taken out in 2024 and made roadworthy at the Classic Center in Fellbach, now said to be the only running four-rotor C111 (the ABS no longer works). Pebble Beach Concours, August 2024; photo shoot at Bosch's Boxberg track, autumn 2024. Comes with its removable luggage tray, matching luggage and two wheel sets.

Auction announced 17-18 November 2026: RM Sotheby's, Louvre, Paris, 3 February 2027. No published estimate; Mercedes aims for "a significant double-digit million amount" to fund the museum's expansion ("Museum 2.0"). Mercedes committed not to sell another C111 for 25 years. Sources: tuningblog.eu, MarketScreener (Nov 2026).

cars.name: C111-IID (diesel)
cars.notes: A C111-II converted to a 3.0 L turbocharged, intercooled OM617 five-cylinder diesel, about 190 hp; pop-up headlights and mirrors removed. Nardò, 12 June 1976: 16 world records in a 64-hour run with four factory drivers, averaging over 155 mph.

cars.name: C111-III
cars.notes: 2 built (a record car and a reserve). Turbo-diesel OM617, about 228-230 hp, drag coefficient about 0.18-0.195, silver. Nardò, April 1978: 9 world records in 12 hours, about 196-200 mph average, drivers Paul Frère, Rico Steinmann, Hans Liebold and Guido Moch. On 30 April the first car burst a tyre and was damaged; the reserve car carried on. One C111-III became the C111-IV.

cars.name: C111-IV
cars.notes: One car, rebuilt from a C111-III. Twin-turbo M117 V8 (4.5 L, enlarged to 4.8 L), about 500 hp, big front spoiler and twin rear fins. Nardò, 5 May 1979: closed-circuit world record of 403.978 km/h (251 mph), driven by Hans Liebold (Wikipedia gives 403.78 km/h).

cars.name: Aston Martin DB4 GT Zagato
cars.notes:
Lighter, shorter DB4 GT bodied by Zagato in Milan. 3.7 L straight-six, about 314 bhp. 25 planned, 19 built 1960-63 (chassis 0176-0191, 0193, 0199, 0200): at £5,470 it cost far more than a Jaguar E-type. Drivers included Stirling Moss, Jim Clark, Innes Ireland and Roy Salvadori. Four were built to lightweight DP207/209 racing spec (0182, 0183, 0191, 0193).

Sanction II (built 1988-91, Aston Martin with RS Williams and Zagato): 4 cars on the unused chassis numbers 0192, 0196, 0197, 0198, each sold for over $1M. Sanction III (2000): 2 cars from spare body shells on DB4 chassis 344 and 424.

Not tracked: the 19 Continuation cars (2019, Aston Martin Works), sold only as a pair with a DBS GT Zagato in the DBZ Centenary Collection.

Records: 2 VEV (0183/R) sold for £10,081,500 at Bonhams Goodwood Festival of Speed, 2018. 0186/R sold for $14.3M at RM Sotheby's New York, December 2015, and went unsold at $11.75M at Monterey in August 2026. Sources: astonmartinzagato.com registry, Wikipedia, Motorsport Magazine, Top Gear, Motor1.

cars.name: DB4 GT Zagato 0183/R "2 VEV"

Crashed heavily at Spa in 1962 and rebuilt to DP209 spec; returned to 1962 spec after a road accident in 1993. Sold for £10,081,500 at Bonhams, Goodwood Festival of Speed, 2018 (a British-car auction record then).
